# Chapter One: Still Of The Night

Ferdinand crouched low in the field; dusk had slowly settled over the land shrouding everything in the waning light of the evening sun. Shadows began to stretch as if reaching out and trying to touch the living. He could hear the shallow raspy tone of his own breath and it felt as if his heart was going to explode out of his chest. Ferdinand took a few deep calming breaths, trying to settle his heart and calm his shaking hands. He scanned the twilight looking for anything out of place, or any movement from the tree line. As he studied the shadows of the bushes and trees, he said a prayer and crossed himself, his armor no longer filled him with the confidence of a second skin as he moved it made small scraping sounds as the joints rubbed together. He winced as it did it again. He knew his quarry had the hearing of a forest predator and would be able to pick out that sound as if it were a beacon alerting them to his location.

He quietly began to take off the Armor, he removed his gloves and laid them on the ground quietly, every time the armor made a sound he would pause to ensure it had not garnered the attention of anything nearby. Ferdinand quickly removed his pauldrons and then his gorget. Exposing his neck and the leather straps for the chest piece. Once he had completed removing his armor, he crouched there with only linen pants and a shirt feeling the cool breeze as it dried his sweat that covered his body and face. His eyes continued to scan the tree line, he knew it was out there, had heard it, that blood curdling sound that commenced the hunt. He never looked down as he felt around and then found his sword and scabbard. The Red Cross on the pommel standing out against the white pearl and gold hilt. He took a good grip on the sword and slowly slid it out of the scabbard. He winced as the sword, in contact with the metal ring at the top of the scabbard began to make a scraping noise, he quickly lifted it a little so it wouldn’t contact the ring.

In a moment the sword was free and in his hand. He felt infinitely better with the weapon ready to use. The bishop who had sent him here had told him this was a group not a single creature and that they hunted as a pack, isolating a victim and once they were away from lights and people, they would pounce. Ferdinand had read the accounts and seen the sketches of what had been left. They were demons, monsters they had attached and mutilated children and women. This was the work of the devil himself.

He said another prayer to Michael to strengthen his resolve. Ferdinand was scared, trembling even; this was not his first hunt; there had been many since he first swore his secret oath all those years ago. He had continued to faithfully serve the church since becoming Emperor. As the years passed he knew this day would come; and it filled his heart with dread; it had been 10 years since his last hunt. As Emperor he had become complacent in his training, Ferdinand was painfully aware that he was not as nimble as he once was. But he was here, once again hunting demons in the dark, fulfilling his Oath; after all being Emperor did not excuse him from his duty; as the Bishop delighted in reminding him.

He had explained that the Pope had sent three hunters after this group and none had returned, He was the last and he carried Lobera, his sword, it was special, but only in his hands so the church had been forced to call upon its greatest hunter, the one they called the Invincible Warrior of Jesus Christ. No one except his most trusted body guard knew and that was only because he had to recruit his friend and guard to assist him in getting out of the castle, Ferdinand fanned himself with his free hand the night was unseasonably warm for Austria in April it was going to be a hot summer he thought. A sound to his left startled him and Ferdinand swung his sword towards it letting out a hiss. The sword made contact loudly with a metal gauntlet and then was lowered by the man who had come upon him “My lord, we see no sign of this thing you speak of, surely it is not here” Said Ulbricht, captain of his guards. Ferdinand shook his head “My friend it has an incredible ability to hide, even for one so large, but mark me it is here and when you least expect it, it will be upon you and with haste. Keep your wits dear friend, I would hate to lose you this night” Ferdinand whispered to his friend and body guard. “Where are the other men” He asked scanning the tree line again.

“They are dispersed along the south line, they were told to be quiet and report anything out of the ordinary.” Ferdinand nodded to himself “What did you tell them” he asked arching an eyebrow at his friend. Ulbricht looked at him a bit sheepishly “I told them a wild boar was loosed in these parts and we were to assist the Emperor in hunting it” He shrugged and looked back towards where the men were spread out “I am not sure they believed it, but they will be vigilant and when the time comes they will strike should you need it sire” Ferdinand nodded “thank you old friend, I know the story is unbelievable, but I have seen these creatures and hunted them before, I do not wish the nightmares I am about to incite upon you, but I needed your help, I am no longer able to take these creatures alone” Ferdinand felt shame when he said it out loud, that is why he was scared. He was older and slower and had not trained in many years. This time he was afraid he would not walk away from this.

“We are here Sire, we will ensure your protection even at the cost of our own lives, should this beast make itself known” Ulbricht stated Ferdinand could see in his eyes, he did not believe his Emperor about the creature. Oh my friend you will soon enough and then you too will not be able to sleep more than a few hours, for that I apologize, I did not wish to pass my burden onto anyone else.

A tortured scream floated over the field from the tree line and Ferdinand broke out in fresh sweat as he listened. Ulbricht tilted his head to focus on where the sound was coming from. “It’s Percival” he exclaimed and took off for the tree line. Ferdinand was right behind him, keeping a death grip on his sword and continuing to scan the tree line. The scream lasted for only about 20 seconds and then abruptly cut off. Only the echo of it floated over the field for a moment, and then the only sound that could be heard was the rushing of feet as he and Ulbricht make their way to the source of the noise. A light out of the corner of Ferdinand’s eye caught his attention, The sword, it had begun to glow in the night air, light at first and then as they approached the glow became brighter. “Ulbricht slow your pace; we are among enemies” he said with a hushed voice. They slowed their pace and now that the scream had stopped it was eerily quiet. The mist had settled upon the fields this night heavier than they usually would have this time of year.

As they neared the forest they could hear a dragging sound somewhere in front of them, it stopped as soon as they got within 20 paces of the forest edge. Ferdinand put a hand against his friend’s chest. “This is my fight, I will need you to stay here In case something happens my friend” Ulbricht was about to protest but he knew the look in the emperors eyes when something was a command and not a suggestion. He bowed his head slightly and stood his ground, as Ferdinand slowly paced forward the sword at the ready. The ground crunched beneath his feet having not rained in many days. His face was slick with sweat. He was afraid, afraid of not being fast or strong enough, it had been too long. And he knew it, the beast could probably smell the fear rippling off his body.

His foot touched upon something slick he pointed the glowing sword down to see the white and red of bloody entrails as they snaked off into the woods. Oh yes the best had been here and had done its evil work. He slowly followed the pieces of bone and meat into the forest. Walking as silently as he could and scanning the forest in front of him. The beast would fear the sword, this he knows, one touch would burn its flesh as one strike would sear through its evil bone and muscle like butter. The creature as all its kind could sense the weapon and the power it commands.

This was one of the power of the hunters, those who commanded holy weapons against such creatures, as he had done for all these years. He heard the crack of a twig to his left and as he turned something large flung through the woods to his right. He heard a guttural chuckle but could not ascertain where it had come from. This was not right, these creatures feared these weapons and those who wielded them, this beast should be running causing Ferdinand to hunt it down. But it stayed, it toyed with him.

“Did you not think that time would catch up to you old man.” The guttural voice said from everywhere at once. Ferdinand stopped cold, this creature could talk, this was not like the ones he had hunted before. He only knew of one creature of this ilk who had the ability to keep its full human wits, a prince, one of the original six touched by Satan himself. But no one had laid eyes on such a creature in centuries.

The sweat dried from his body as fear fully took hold of him. This was not a normal hunt, nor a normal creature. “Show yourself demon, for I know what you are” he said into the night with as much gusto as he could muster. And that eerie cold rough chuckle came from the woods again, mocking him with its inability to be sourced. “You will die creature as those of your ilk have before at my hands” Ferdinand said into the forest as he slowly circled, looking for any signs of the creature. Another branch snapped and behind him he could feel claws rake across his back as something large passed him. He swung his sword, missing whatever it had been by mere inches. The pain on his back was excruciating but helped to better clear his mind. “Sire do you require assistance” Ulbricht yelled, Ferdinand could hear the voices of the other men around him probably having come from their own positions upon hearing his yelling. “NO, stay where you are” he said with all the authority he could muster. “That’s right old man, this is your fight, as it has been for many years, they would just get in the way” The creatures guttural tongue taunted him.

Suddenly he remembered, why was he playing to this beast, the sword was not the only weapon he possessed. He closed his eyes and said an Aramaic incantation, when he opened them, they glowed and he could see as if it were daylight, and three in the distance outlined in red was the creature. It was the biggest one he had ever seen. Lord it was huge. It moved with a speed that Ferdinand could barely see as his eyes tracked it, He closed them again and began to say another incantation that would give him the strength he needed to defeat the best. But that had been his undoing, before he could finish, He felt a searing pain in his had and opened his eyes to see that is arm was gone, as was the sword.

Ferdinand opened his mouth to scream when a large set of teeth descended and clamped around his shoulder. It dragged him off quickly as he screamed and screamed.

Ulbricht could take no more, he ordered his men into the forest. They spread out and searched for their king. All they found was the arm and the sword. By daybreak they had all but given up. Ulbricht ordered them to keep searching, he wrapped the arm and sword in his own tunic and rode back for Vienna, the Bishop would want to know what happened.

IT took him a full day of riding to reach the chapel where the bishop was housed. He dismounted his horse and entered the chamber where the bishop was writing in a book.

Angrily he flipped open his tunic and the arm and sword rolled across the desk of the bishop. “I don’t know you name sir, or what power you have over my king, but this is all that is left. I ask that you let us form a full contingent and search for him immediately.

The bishop stared at the arm thoughtfully and asked Ulbricht to recite the story exactly as he remembered it. He started at the beginning at by the end the old Bishop looked very troubled. All he said was “A prince took a king” and then shook his head. Ulbricht recited his demand for the full contingent and the old Bishop nodded his head. “No the King died peacefully in his bed in Vienna, the whole of the country will mourn and not a word of this will be spoken, do you understand me Ulbricht. He said with a forceful tone. Ulbricht protested and the Bishop produced a ring and a letter, he handed them to Ulbricht to read then, and then reread them. 
“This is from the king” he said in awe 
“Yes my son”, said the bishop, “giving me full authority to handle this matter the way I see fit, do you understand “

Ulbricht nodded, what would you have me do. The bishop took the sword and put it in a box, where he handed it to a lower clergy who quickly disappeared, from under his desk he produced another which looked quite like the other he had just whisked away. “You are you ride this night, carry this sword and this letter to Don Yuan Manuel, he will know what to do, other than that you are not to speak to anyone about this, do you understand. Ulbricht hung his head and nodded, he would comply with his kings last wished
